questions.text:
Let [latex]G=(V,E)[/latex] be an undirected unweighted connected graph. The diameter of [latex]G[/latex] is defined as:
[latex]diam(G)=\displaystyle \max_{u,v \in V} \{ \text{the length of shortest path between }u \text{ and }v \}[/latex]

Let [latex]M[/latex] be the adjacency matrix of [latex]G[/latex].
Define graph [latex]G_2[/latex] on the same set of vertices with adjacency matrix [latex]N[/latex], where

[latex]N_{ij}=\left\{\begin{array} {lcl} 1 &\text{if}\; M_{ij}>0 \text{ or } P_{ij}>0, \text{ where }P=M^2\\0 &\text{otherwise} \end{array}\right.[/latex]

Which one of the following statements is true?
questions.solution:
[latex]P=M^2[/latex] has [latex]P_{ij} \gt 0[/latex] exactly when there is a path of length 2. So in [latex]G_2[/latex], u and v are adjacent whenever their distance in G is 1 or 2.

A shortest path of length d in G can be covered with [latex]\lceil d/2\rceil[/latex] such jumps, so [latex]diam(G_2)=\lceil diam(G)/2\rceil[/latex].

Answer: [latex]diam(G_2)\le\lceil diam(G)/2\rceil[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: [latex]diam(G_2)\leq \left \lceil diam(G)/2 \right \rceil[/latex]
[latex]\left \lceil diam(G)/2 \right \rceil \lt diam(G_2) \lt diam(G)[/latex]
[latex]diam(G_2) =diam(G)[/latex]
[latex]diam(G) \lt diam(G_2) \leq 2 \; diam(G)[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the following language:

[latex]L= \{ w \in \{0,1\}^* \mid w \text{ ends with the substring } 011 \}[/latex]

Which one of the following deterministic finite automata accepts [latex]L[/latex]?
questions.solution:
States should remember the longest suffix matching a prefix of 011: q0 (nothing), q1 ("0"), q2 ("01"), q3 ("011", final).

From the final state: on 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] q1 (suffix "0"), on 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] q0 (suffix "0111" has no useful part).
- (A) and (B) loop on 1 at the final state, accepting 0111 False
- (C) goes from the final state to q2 on 1, accepting 01111 False
- (D) has exactly the transitions above True

Answer: D

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: A
B
C
D

questions.text:
For a Turing machine M, < M > denotes an encoding of M. Consider the following two languages.

[latex]\begin{array}{ll} L1 = \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ takes more than } 2021 \text{ steps on all inputs} \} \\ L2 = \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M\text{ takes more than } 2021 \text{ steps on some input} \} \end{array}[/latex]

Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.solution:
In 2021 steps, M can read at most the first 2021 input symbols. So "more than 2021 steps" depends only on inputs of length up to 2021, a finite set.

Simulate M for 2022 steps on each such input; this decides both "on all inputs" (L1) and "on some input" (L2).

Answer: Both L1 and L2 are decidable

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both L1 and L2 are decidable.
L1 is decidable  and L2 is undecidable.
L1 is undecidable  and L2 is decidable.
Both L1 and L2 are undecidable.

questions.text:
Define [latex]R_n[/latex] to be the maximum amount earned by cutting a rod of length n meters into one or more pieces of integer length and selling them. For [latex]i > 0[/latex], let [latex]p[i][/latex] denote the selling price of a rod whose length is [latex]i[/latex] meters. Consider the array of prices:

[latex]\text{p}[1]=1,\text{p}[2]=5,\text{p}[3]=8,\text{p}[4]=9,\text{p}[5]=10,\text{p}[6]=17,\text{p}[7]=18[/latex]

which of the following statements is/are correct about [latex]R_7[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Best values: R1 = 1, R2 = 5, R3 = 8, R4 = 10 (2+2), R5 = 13 (2+3), R6 = 17, R7 = 18.

R7 = 18 is reached by:
- one piece of 7 (18)
- 6 + 1 (17 + 1)
- 2 + 2 + 3 (5 + 5 + 8)

Three different solutions, one of which has three pieces (so option 4 is false).

Answer: [latex]R_7=18[/latex] and it is achieved by three different solutions
